sentences.show: For fifteen months, planes fed half a city. And one pilot bombed it with chocolate.
It ended on this day in 1949.
Stalin had blocked every road and railway into West Berlin.
But the air corridors stayed open.
So American and British planes flew in food, and coal.
At the peak, a plane arrived every thirty seconds.
Pilot Gail Halvorsen met children at the airport fence.
He had just two sticks of gum.
They shared them, and sniffed the wrappers.
He promised to drop more, and to wiggle his wings.
He tied chocolate to handkerchief parachutes.
Soon, over 23 tons of candy fell on Berlin.
Years earlier, many of these pilots had bombed German cities.
Now Berlin's children called him Uncle Wiggly Wings.
